input.quote: 2.2 Vendor will be Customer's sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services throughout the term.
input.rationale: Section 2.2 imposes a sole-supplier obligation on us covering hosted analytics services for the entire term, with no category narrowing beyond that, no 12-month limit and no automatic exit on Vendor's service level or delivery failures — i.e. exclusive dealing for the full term with no performance-based exit, which is walk-away territory under the rule and fails the fallback. Sections 2.1 (no minimum or purchase commitment) and 12.3 (Vendor acknowledges no exclusivity commitment) contradict 2.2, so the redline both reaches the preferred position (non-exclusive supply) and resolves the internal conflict.

proposal.summary: Make Vendor a non-exclusive provider, removing the sole-supplier commitment on Customer
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot commit to a sole-supplier arrangement, so we have made Vendor a non-exclusive provider; this also removes the conflict with Sections 2.1 and 12.3, which confirm we have given no exclusivity or minimum-volume commitment.

ops.oldText: 2.2 Vendor will be Customer's sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services throughout the term.
ops.newText: 2.2 Vendor will be a non-exclusive provider of hosted analytics services, and Customer may procure the same or similar services from any third party at any time.
